key_insight: A spherical ciliate model with filament oscillators shows how local cilium stiffness can switch collective beating between symplectic-like and diaplectic metachronal waves, which in turn changes propulsion efficiency.
engineering_relevance: The results provide design insight for synthetic cilia and active surface actuators, showing how tuning stiffness and beat geometry can control emergent coordination, swimming speed, and rotation.
method: Represent each cilium with two degrees of freedom: a phase along a prescribed beat sequence and an orientation angle.
Simulate cilia distributed over a sphere to compute emergent coordination and the resulting fluid-driven propulsion.
Vary cilium stiffness and beat-plane tilt to study transitions between wave states, flow fields, and rotation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical comparisons across stiffness values and beat-plane tilt, evaluating emergent wave type, propulsion efficiency, flow fields, and swimming speed.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on a simplified filament oscillator model, so real ciliary geometry, compliance, and hydrodynamic coupling may shift the predicted wave transition threshold.
paper_title: Emergent coordination and propulsion of a model spherical ciliate
